title: Theology close
hook: belief is reasoned about, but lived in the heart
tomorrow: I was sent to perfect character

segments.voice: Yesterday, mercy's hundred parts, and your line: ninety-nine kept for that day. Did you get to your act of mercy, carefully? Today the week ends, and so does this whole block on belief. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-seven.

Some desert Arabs came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and announced: we believe. The Qur'an records the answer he was told to give them, and it's gentle but firm. Don't say you believe. Say you've submitted. Faith hasn't yet entered your hearts. It's a striking line to end a block of theology on. For weeks we've talked about what Muslims believe and how theologians argued about it. And here the Qur'an says belief isn't finished when you can say it. It has to go somewhere. Today, the theology close.
screen: `WE BELIEVE, THEY SAID.` → `SAY RATHER: WE SUBMIT.` → `FAITH HAS TO ENTER THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Look back at the road. The block opened with the six articles of faith: Allah the One, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day, and the decree. Then the theologians: kalam, the Mu'tazilah and their justice, the trial over the created Qur'an, al-Ash'ari and al-Maturidi, the Athari approach, Shia theology, and the hard question of suffering. Then the unseen journey: death and return, the grave, the questions, the trumpet, the gathering, the book, the scale, the bridge, and this week, the intercession, the pool, the fire, the garden, seeing Him, and mercy in a hundred parts. That's a lot of reasoning. The theologians argued hard, and argued well, and disagreed with each other in earnest. Their work is still studied. But the verse about the desert Arabs puts it in its place. Saying it is one step. Faith entering the heart is another. A hadith in Sahih Muslim gives the other half of the picture. Faith, the Prophet said, has many branches. The highest is saying there is no god but Allah. The lowest is moving something harmful out of the road. And modesty is a branch of faith too. Notice the range. The top branch is a creed. The bottom branch is a rock on a path, moved so nobody trips. That's the bridge between this block and the next. Belief is reasoned about, but lived. Starting tomorrow, the path turns inward, to character and the heart's stations: what belief looks like in a person.
screen: `SIX ARTICLES, THE THEOLOGIANS, THE UNSEEN.` · `SAYING IT IS ONE STEP.` · `FROM A CREED TO A ROCK IN THE ROAD.` · then, large: `REASONED ABOUT, BUT LIVED.`

segments.voice: The practice: two units of prayer. If you pray, you can pray two rak'ahs now, a voluntary prayer, slowly, as you've been taught, letting each movement carry what you've learned in this block. If you don't pray, or can't right now, sit quietly instead. Settle, and breathe. Let one belief from these weeks come to mind, whichever one stayed with you. Then ask one plain question: where would this show up in my hands today? Not in an argument. In a hand on a door, a word to a neighbor, a rock moved off a path. Rest there. The bell holds the time.
Theology close. The end of a block on belief: the articles, the theologians, the unseen journey, and a reminder that faith is reasoned about, but has to be lived. Today's word.

Your line: believe, and live it. Today, move one obstacle out of someone's way, on a sidewalk, in an inbox, anywhere. Tomorrow, a new block: I was sent to perfect character. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims study the articles of faith and the questions of theology, and teachers also stress that faith shows in deeds; Muslims may also pray two voluntary rak'ahs outside the five daily prayers.

myth: in the Qur'an, saying 'we believe' settles the matter of faith
the desert Arabs were told faith had not yet entered their hearts.
the hadith counts moving something harmful from the road as a branch of faith

modesty is named in the hadith as a branch of faith
the same hadith says modesty is a branch of faith.

fork.setup: you've just told the Prophet: we believe. what does the Qur'an have him answer?
options: say rather: we submit; faith has not yet entered your hearts.
fork.reveal: the answer is gentle but firm: belief has to enter the heart, not only the mouth.

original.note: Arabic: faith; the word the desert Arabs claimed too soon.

trapdoor: what you thought: theology is about getting the beliefs right.
what it means: belief is reasoned about with care, and has to enter the heart and show in deeds.
what a scholar hears: the iman and islam distinction in 49:14, and the branches-of-faith hadith joining creed to conduct.
